**Predecessor release:** v3.2.7 (**LOCKED release of record**, Robin 2026-10-20: "I lock it"; a point release on v3.2.6, label assigned by Robin 2026-10-20: "its a point upgrade, so update it to v3.2.7"). Relative to v3.2.7, this release applies the reviewed successor corrections: the integrated corrections of 2026-10-24 and repair topics 1–14, as 292 replacement hunks declared against the pinned v3.2.7 bytes in `kernel/successor/CORRECTIONS.json` (290 excluding the two header hunks; including the footer metadata hunk and the 2026-10-24 integrated corrections) and recorded in `kernel/successor/repairs/` (summary in the v3.3.0 changelog below). Item standings, limitations and not-claimed clauses are as recorded in the item tags and the post-v3.2.5 concordance (Part VII); no status is upgraded, and no Goldbach, RH/Landau or centered-comb standing is raised.

**Release scope:** Unsupported universal statements are withdrawn or scoped rather than retained as theorems; all 186 native item identities and their order are kept. Where the text below says "successor draft", it means this release's text as changed from v3.2.7. Eight declared, reviewed replacements change text that was item-locked in v3.2.7 (a complete list, derived by script from the item-locked fold spans recorded in `kernel/next/ITEMS.json`): in the Farey II.5g–k fold, REPAIR14-A-11 (census line), REPAIR-HUNK-041 and REPAIR-HUNK-042 (rupture-and-repair record: "order" read as "admissible denominator"); in Goldbach II.23.5c–e, REPAIR-HUNK-133 (Def–Prop II.23.5d Status paragraph), REPAIR-HUNK-134 (Def II.23.5e defining sentence: $\Lambda_G(r)$ is defined for any positive integer $r$, its comparator use staying at even $N \ge 4$) and REPAIR14-PR60-LAMBDAG (Def II.23.5e displays); in II.23.9, REPAIR14-C-02-POINTER (Def II.23.9 parameter pointer) and REPAIR-HUNK-146 (Rmk II.23.9b shell-swap gloss). Their historical attestations and item locks cover the original bytes only, and this release does not renew them. No status is upgraded. Eleven native tags change against v3.2.7, each by a reviewed correction: Thm 6.2, Thm 8.14a and Thm 8.20h.3 are withdrawn to open (proved/unconditional to conditional/open) and Rmk 8.20h.4 is downgraded (unconditional to open); Rmk 9.7z splits its label (the iff becomes κ-palindromic sufficiency, with necessity open), and Rmk 1.2 and Rmk 3.6 split theirs into unconditional and interpretive parts; Def 5.1, Def 5.2, Rmk 9.4a and Note 9.4b change their dependency lists only. The v3.3.0 release standing covers the assembled kernel as a whole; it does not re-attest the edited item-locked text.

It supersedes v3.2.7 (SHA-256 `b8266896dad305356faa76c7248338d3aed37115f8c434f7727475f28ad42a81`, LOCKED by Robin 2026-10-20: "I lock it"); v3.2.7 superseded v3.2.6 (SHA-256 `4a23d62e15ada3819defe6919e56fe9f2ef6a9a10eb7f5c4082e4b6b442cdb94`, locked by Robin 2026-10-12), which superseded v3.2.5 (SHA-256 `ac53e75b73c42f185248464e3daf856a3dd3fd98b56dfff971341b80b10717ef`). Relative to v3.2.7, this release applies the reviewed successor corrections: the integrated corrections of 2026-10-24 and repair topics 1–14, as 292 replacement hunks declared against the pinned v3.2.7 bytes in `kernel/successor/CORRECTIONS.json` (290 excluding the two header hunks; including the footer metadata hunk and the 2026-10-24 integrated corrections) and recorded in `kernel/successor/repairs/` (summary in the v3.3.0 changelog below). Item standings, limitations and not-claimed clauses are as recorded in the item tags and the post-v3.2.5 concordance (Part VII); no status is upgraded, and no Goldbach, RH/Landau or centered-comb standing is raised.

**Release scope:** Unsupported universal statements are withdrawn or scoped rather than retained as theorems; all 186 native item identities and their order are kept. Where the text below says "successor draft", it means this release's text as changed from v3.2.7. Twenty-two declared, reviewed replacements change text that was item-locked in v3.2.7; the list is complete with respect to five lock sources: (a) item-locked folds in `kernel/next/ITEMS.json`, (b) native-tag lock fields, (c) in-body item-lock records, (d) version-history item-lock records and (e) bodies described as locked; all 108 lock-word occurrences in the v3.2.7 kernel are classified (`docs/releases/v3.3.0/scripts/locked_span_intersections_v2.py`): in the Farey II.5g–k fold, REPAIR14-A-11, REPAIR-HUNK-041 and REPAIR-HUNK-042; in Goldbach II.23.5c–e, REPAIR-HUNK-133, REPAIR-HUNK-134 (Def II.23.5e defining sentence: $\Lambda_G(r)$ for any positive integer $r$, comparator use at even $N \ge 4$) and REPAIR14-PR60-LAMBDAG; in II.23.9, REPAIR14-C-02-POINTER and REPAIR-HUNK-146; in Thm II.3c, REPAIR-HUNK-024; in Rmk II.5f, REPAIR-HUNK-040; in Rmk 9.7z, REPAIR-HUNK-101 to REPAIR-HUNK-109; in Note 14.5, REPAIR-HUNK-230; in Cor 14.5a, REPAIR-HUNK-231 and REPAIR14-D-09. Two of these correct the mathematics of locked statements: REPAIR-HUNK-040 (Rmk II.5f(i): "the path graph on $V$" becomes the induced subgraph on $V$ of the integer path, generally a union of paths) and REPAIR-HUNK-101 to REPAIR-HUNK-109 (Rmk 9.7z: the locked iff is weakened to sufficiency, with necessity open; its lock record is relabelled "Historical lock"). Separately, under source (e), Lemma 9.7a (REPAIR-HUNK-087 to REPAIR-HUNK-089) and Rmk 9.7h (REPAIR-HUNK-112 to REPAIR-HUNK-114) are described as locked (v3.1.21 "three locked bodies"), lock scope not recorded; Note 9.3a.1 has no hits. The historical attestations and item locks of all these items cover the original bytes only, and this release does not renew them. No status is upgraded. Eleven native tags change against v3.2.7, each by a reviewed correction: Thm 6.2, Thm 8.14a and Thm 8.20h.3 are withdrawn to open (proved/unconditional to conditional/open) and Rmk 8.20h.4 is downgraded (unconditional to open); in Rmk 9.7z the iff is weakened to sufficiency (necessity open); Rmk 1.2 and Rmk 3.6 split their labels into unconditional and interpretive parts; Def 5.1, Def 5.2, Rmk 9.4a and Note 9.4b change their dependency lists only. The v3.3.0 release standing covers the assembled kernel as a whole; it does not re-attest the edited item-locked text.
